title: Probe, AVFoundation part: MP4/MOV write/read (AVAssetWriter/AVAssetReader) and headless camera movie recording
status: host-tested and compiled for iOS arm64; NOT run on the phone
done: probe/av/probe_objc.h: hand-written Objective-C runtime (objc_getClass, sel_registerName, objc_msgSend with a per-call-site cast to the exact C signature, objc_msgSend_stret on x86_64, objc_autoreleasePoolPush/Pop, objc_allocateClassPair/class_addMethod/objc_registerClassPair), the global-block literal struct and the N2O_GLOBAL_BLOCK macro (isa=&_NSConcreteGlobalBlock, flags=1<<28, descriptor), libdispatch semaphores, and the CoreMedia audio + CoreVideo pool declarations that include/n2_apple.h does not carry. No Apple SDK header is included.

probe/av/probe_av.c: T10 'av.write.h264.aac' writes /private/var/db/nord2-video/t10.mp4 with AVFileTypeMPEG4 ('public.mpeg-4'), a 640x480 @ 1 Mbit/s 'avc1' AVAssetWriterInput plus AVAssetWriterInputPixelBufferAdaptor (420v attributes), 60 synthetic pictures at pts i/30, a 44100 Hz mono 64 kbit/s AAC audio input fed with 2 s of a 440 Hz 16-bit LPCM sine in CMSampleBuffers (88200 samples, 87 buffers: 86x1024 + 136), markAsFinished, finishWritingWithCompletionHandler: waited on a 15 s dispatch semaphore; reports writer status, NSError description and file size key by key.
probe/av/probe_av.c: T10b the same with 'hvc1' to t10b.mov with AVFileTypeQuickTimeMovie ('com.apple.quicktime-movie').

probe/av/probe_av.c: T11 'av.read' opens t10.mp4 with AVURLAsset, reports tracks, naturalSize, duration and nominalFrameRate; AVAssetReader with an AVAssetReaderTrackOutput (420v) counts decoded frames (expects 60) and reports the mean luma of the first picture; a second output with LPCM settings counts decoded audio samples.

probe/av/probe_av.c: T12 'av.capture.movie' is skipped with result 2 unless <db>/nord2-video-probe-camera exists; otherwise it builds AVCaptureSession (PresetHigh, fallback 1280x720), the default video device and its input, an AVCaptureMovieFileOutput, starts, records 3 s to t12.mov, stops, waits 10 s for a delegate class built at run time (objc_allocateClassPair + class_addMethod for captureOutput:didFinishRecordingToOutputFileURL:fromConnections:error:), reports authorizationStatusForMediaType:, each step, the error and the file size, then reads the movie back.
probe/av/probe_av.c: T12a the same with the audio device/input added (key t12a.audio=on).
Every message that can return nil is checked by name before use (writer/inputs/adaptor/device/session/output/URLs/strings). Each test pushes and pops an autorelease pool.

All AVFileType*/AVMediaType*/AVVideo*Key*/AVFormatIDKey*/AVSampleRateKey*/AVNumberOfChannelsKey*/AVEncoderBitRateKey*/AVLinearPCM*Key*/AVCaptureSessionPreset* and kCVPixelBuffer*Key values are read at run time via dlsym(RTLD_DEFAULT, name) and *(id *)slot; the literal in probe_av.c is used only when dlsym returns NULL and is then reported as <test>.const.<symbol>=literal:<value>. The host oracle asserts that no fallback happened.

probe/av/symbols.txt: the exact iOS imports (libobjc, CoreMedia, CoreVideo, CoreFoundation, libSystem incl. __NSConcreteGlobalBlock and libdispatch); checked with sdk/make_tbds.py into a private directory: every undefined symbol of the arm64 object is covered except _probe_say and _probe_fill_nv12, which WP07's probe/probe_core.c defines at link.

probe/av/test/fake_objc.c + fake_objc.h + t_av.c: a made-up Objective-C runtime with an x86_64 assembly objc_msgSend/objc_msgSend_stret that records every (receiver class, selector, class-vs-instance), returns scripted objects and records the settings dictionaries. Host oracle checks: exact T10 writer selector sequence (including 60 appendPixelBuffer:withPresentationTime: and 87 appendSampleBuffer:), scripted startWriting=NO returns 1 with the scripted error and sends no append, the literal 640/480/1000000/'avc1' and 1633772320/44100/1/64000 settings, both inputs set to expectsMediaDataInRealTime=NO, T11 60 frames + 128.00 luma + 88200 audio samples + 640x480/2.000 s/30.00 fps, T12 returns 2 and sends zero messages without the switch, T12/T12a with the switch complete the delegate, the 1000-byte file and the read-back.

probe/av/run_tests.sh: builds and runs the host oracle with -std=c11 -O2 -g -Wall -Wextra -Werror -fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-sanitize-recover=undefined, then compiles probe_av.c for arm64-apple-ios16.0 with the PLAN.md 4.3 flags and fails if the compiler prints anything.
The iOS arm64 object build is warning-free and the host oracle is ASan+UBSan clean.

Integration: after the lead's probe_core/stdio fixes, probe/{core,main,vt,img,audio}.c + probe/av/probe_av.c compile with build_ios.sh's flags and ld64.lld links build/WP06/probe/n2vt_probe (Mach-O 64-bit arm64 executable, 148112 bytes, 160 imports) against the generated TBDs with no -U exception.

The three LPCM boolean settings (AVLinearPCMIsFloatKey/BigEndianKey/NonInterleaved) are NSNumber/CFBoolean values from +[NSNumber numberWithBool:], not CFNumbers from numberWithInt:, because AVFoundation validates those keys as CFBoolean.

The lead's own stage-0 build with AV sources enabled succeeds: STAGE_AV=1 bash gpu/video/install/build_stage0.sh build/WP06/stage0-av -> Slim.videoencoder 68416 B (sha256 ee604d61...), n2vt_probe 148176 B (sha256 c2ebd736...). This is the exact build the lead would install; it copies probe/av/*.c + probe_objc.h + symbols.txt and links them.
not_done: T10, T10b, T11, T12 and T12a have never been run on the phone. No claim is made that AVFoundation accepts these selectors, settings or constants; only that the code compiles for arm64 and that the host oracle's ordering/nil handling is right.

The dlsym symbol names of the AVFoundation/CoreVideo constants have not been checked against the dyld shared cache (the lead can; the cache work directory is not visible here). The host fake resolves all of them by construction.

T12/T12a require the switch file /private/var/db/nord2-video-probe-camera and the camera TCC row; both are the lead's install work (stage 4). The probe only reports authorizationStatusForMediaType:; it does not call requestAccessForMediaType: (no UI on the phone).
The 15 s finishWriting timeout path is not exercised by the host oracle (the fake always calls the completion handler); a timeout only sets t10.finish=0 and fails the test.
T10 does not call startSessionAtSourceTime:; AVAssetWriter starts the session at the first appended sample. This is deliberate and reported here, not hidden.
T10b needs the HEVC encoder registered by the plug-in (WP05/lead); if it is absent, startWriting or the appends fail and t10b.* says where. The probe does not skip T10b on that account.

No Objective-C exception is caught in C. Every nil-returning call is checked, but an NSException raised by AVFoundation in-process reaches the probe runner's forked child and is reported as result 'crash' by probe_core.c. That is the task's accepted containment, not a substitute for the nil checks.
The real-time behaviour of the H.264 encoder under CMCapture (ProfileLevel and RealTime properties, dropped frames) is WP05's and the lead's area; T12 only measures what the capture graph does.

The CVPixelBufferPool path (adaptor.pixelBufferPool + CVPixelBufferPoolCreatePixelBuffer) is exercised by the host fake; on the phone it is unverified whether the adaptor offers a pool for 420v and whether its buffer attributes match.
Only 420v input/output is attempted. No BGRA, 420f, i420, 10-bit or non-square-pixel path.
The probe accepts a test-only N2_PROBE_DB environment variable to relocate /private/var/db (used by the host oracle); on the phone it is unset, so the task's exact paths are used.
The audio is 2.000 s exactly (88200 samples) in 87 CMSampleBuffers; the last one carries 136 samples, not 1024. The task said '1024 frames each'; this is stated rather than padded to 89088 samples.

The probe is a short-lived process and does not send -release to the objects it owns from +alloc/-init (AVAssetReaderTrackOutput outputs, AVCaptureSession, AVCaptureMovieFileOutput, the run-time delegate). They die with the process; this is deliberate, and the host fake keeps its objects in static arrays so ASan/LSan have nothing to report.

Stage 0 measured no working H.264 encoder on the phone yet (VTCompressionSessionCreate succeeds, the first frame returns -12908), so T10 is expected to fail until WP05 registers n2avc; T11 then fails at t11.track.video=0 because t10.mp4 is absent. That is the intended cascade, not an AVFoundation result. T10b (HEVC) is independent and is expected to be the useful writer result before n2avc lands.

deviations_from_task_text: The delegate selector is captureOutput:didFinishRecordingToOutputFileAtURL:fromConnections:error: (with 'At'), not ...ToOutputFileURL... as in TASK.md. Evidence: the exact string is in the phone's dyld cache (AVFCapture) and the task's spelling is not; AVCaptureFileOutputRecordingDelegate documents the AtURL form.

AVAsset has tracksWithMediaType: (plural, returns NSArray), not trackWithMediaType:; the phone's dyld cache contains tracksWithMediaType: and not the singular. T11 now takes objectAtIndex:0 after a count check.

The LPCM audio settings key is AVLinearPCMIsNonInterleaved (no 'Key' suffix), unlike AVLinearPCMBitDepthKey/AVLinearPCMIsFloatKey/AVLinearPCMIsBigEndianKey. The cache has exactly that spelling; TASK.md did not enumerate this key, it was my extrapolation and is now corrected.

known_risks: The three selector/constant spellings above were checked against the phone's dyld cache by substring (read-only) and corrected; every other selector name is from the public API and the host fake, not from an export-trie lookup. A wrong selector at run time shows as 'crash' (unrecognized selector) in the forked child, not as a nil return.

Selector spellings, argument shapes and constant symbol names are written from the documented public API, not read out of the cache. A wrong name fails at the first T10 step (reported by key) or makes dlsym fall back to a literal (reported as .const.<symbol>), but it can also make AVFoundation return nil with a confusing error.

The hand-built global block literal (isa=&_NSConcreteGlobalBlock, flags=1<<28, descriptor {0,sizeof(struct n2o_block)}) is the documented block ABI but has not been run on arm64; if the block is not invoked, T10 reports t10.finish=0 after 15 s. The same applies to dispatch_semaphore_wait(dispatch_time(NOW, 15 s)).

T12's delegate class type encoding v48@0:8@16@24@32@40 and the four object arguments of captureOutput:didFinishRecordingToOutputFileURL:fromConnections:error: are from the public AVFoundation API; a mismatch on arm64 would show as a crash in the forked child, not as a clean t12.delegate=0.

The audio path uses CMSampleBufferCreateReady with numSampleSizeEntries=0 and NULL sample sizes (CoreMedia derives 2 bytes/sample from the ASBD); AVAssetWriter might ask for a sample-size array on some versions. The host fake cannot see this.
CFRelease is used on the audio format description, block buffers and sample buffers; the ownership rules are the documented Create/Copy ones but are unverified on the phone.

The AAC encoder behind AVAssetWriterInput is AudioToolbox's; T10 only measures that the writer reaches status 2 and that T11 reads the audio back. If the phone's stock AAC encoder is absent, t10.status/t10.error says so.
T12 records with the default camera device and the PresetHigh (fallback 1280x720) format; it does not pin a format, frame rate or stabilization. The camera agent's plist work may interact with this.
The probe uses 640x480 for the writer tests: enough for C1/C2 but not a 720p/1080p speed measurement (that is WP07's T03).
The host fake's objc_msgSend is x86_64 SysV assembly; it validates ordering and nil handling only. It is not part of the iOS build.
